trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Lisbon, Portugal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour
experiences.description: Spend a culinary afternoon at the iconic Time Out Market, sampling the best of Portuguese cuisine including bacalhau (salted cod), pastéis de nata, piri-piri chicken, and local cheeses. Chat with vendors and discover the stories behind each dish.

experiences.name: Belém Historical Landmarks & Pastéis de Belém
experiences.description: Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery and the iconic Tower of Belém, both masterpieces of Manueline architecture dating to the Age of Discovery. Finish with a visit to the original Pastéis de Belém bakery, open since 1837, for the world-famous custard tarts.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and take the Metro (Red Line from Aeroporto) to central Lisbon for approximately €1.50. Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Alfama neighbourhood on foot — wander the narrow cobblestone streets, admire the colourful tiled facades, and climb up to the Miradouro das Portas do Sol viewpoint for sweeping views over the city and the Tagus River. Entry is free and the walk is one of Lisbon's most authentic experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Baixa-Chiado, Lisbon's lively downtown district. Browse the pedestrianised Rua Augusta and take in the iconic Arco da Rua Augusta arch (free to view from outside). Settle in for a relaxed first evening getting your bearings.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and a pastel de nata (custard tart) at a local café near the airport or hotel upon arrival — budget around €2–3.
meals.lunch: Pick up a budget-friendly bifana (pork sandwich) or a prego (steak roll) from a local tasca near Alfama for around €3–5.
meals.dinner: Try A Tasca do Chico or a similar neighbourhood tasca in Alfama for a hearty prato do dia (dish of the day), typically €8–12 including bread, olives, and a glass of house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 13:00 arrival. Purchase a rechargeable Viva Viagem card at the airport Metro station (€0.50 card fee) and load it with credit for cost-effective transport throughout the trip. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for Alfama's hilly cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the São Jorge Castle (Castelo de São Jorge) first thing to beat the crowds. This Moorish hilltop fortress offers panoramic views of Lisbon and the Tagus. Entry is approximately €15 for adults, but the surrounding free public terraces and gardens offer nearly identical views at no cost — a great budget option.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the iconic Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour experience at Mercado da Ribeira in Cais do Sodré. Sample the best of Portuguese cuisine including fresh seafood, traditional petiscos (small bites), local cheeses, and wine from award-winning vendors. This is an ideal way to taste a wide variety of local food in one afternoon without committing to a single expensive restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Ribeira waterfront promenade (Avenida 24 de Julho) as the sun sets over the Tagus. Enjoy the lively atmosphere of the Cais do Sodré and Pink Street (Rua Nova do Carvalho) area.

meals.breakfast: Start the day at a local padaria (bakery) near the hotel — fresh bread roll, butter, and coffee for around €2–3.
meals.lunch: Budget for tasting plates at the Time Out Market as part of the afternoon food tour experience — allocate €15–20 for a satisfying spread of Portuguese specialties.
meals.dinner: Visit a traditional cervejaria (beer hall) near Cais do Sodré for grilled sardines or bacalhau (salt cod) with potatoes — expect to spend €10–14 for a full meal with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: The Time Out Market is busiest on weekend afternoons — arrive early in the afternoon to get the best selection and avoid the longest queues. The market itself is free to enter; you pay only for what you eat. Keep an eye out for the cheaper stalls offering traditional petiscos at lower price points.

day_by_day.morning: Take Tram 28E (one of Lisbon's most famous historic trams) from Martim Moniz through Alfama, Graça, and Estrela — a scenic and authentic way to see the city for just the cost of a Metro/tram fare (~€3). Ride it to the Basílica da Estrela, a stunning 18th-century baroque church with free entry, and explore the surrounding Jardim da Estrela park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Belém Historical Landmarks: explore the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture (entry ~€10, or free on Sunday mornings until 14:00 — aim to arrive before 14:00 to save money). Walk along the riverside to see the iconic Tower of Belém (entry ~€6) and the Monument to the Discoveries (exterior free).
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon via the riverside walk or bus. Explore the Príncipe Real neighbourhood, known for its charming squares, antique shops, and relaxed local vibe. Visit the Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara viewpoint at dusk for beautiful city views — completely free.

meals.breakfast: Stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery in Belém (open since 1837) for the original pastel de Belém custard tarts — €1.20–1.50 each, best enjoyed with a bica (espresso) for a total of around €3–4.
meals.lunch: Pick up a lunch special (prato do dia) at a local tasca near Belém for €8–10, including soup, main course, and a drink.
meals.dinner: Head to a tasca in Príncipe Real or Bairro Alto for traditional caldo verde (green soup) and grilled chicken or pork — budget €10–13 for a full dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Jerónimos Monastery offers free entry on Sunday mornings until 14:00 — this is a significant saving and highly recommended. Belém is about 6 km from central Lisbon; take Bus 728 or Tram 15E from Praça da Figueira (included in your Viva Viagem card). Bring a light jacket as the riverside can be breezy.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Museu Nacional do Azulejo (National Tile Museum), dedicated to Portugal's iconic azulejo ceramic tile tradition. Entry is approximately €5 and the museum is housed in a beautiful former convent. This is one of Lisbon's most unique and underrated cultural experiences, deeply tied to Portuguese history and identity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mouraria neighbourhood, the oldest and most historically significant district in Lisbon — the birthplace of Fado music. Explore the Intendente square and the free outdoor murals and cultural spaces. Head to the Museu do Fado (Fado Museum) for an affordable deep-dive into the history of Portugal's soulful national music genre (entry ~€5).
day_by_day.evening: Experience a live Fado performance at a traditional Fado house (casa de fado) in Alfama or Mouraria. Many venues offer free Fado nights or low-cover shows (€5–10) earlier in the evening — check listings for A Tasca do Chico or Mesa de Frades for authentic, intimate performances.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a coffee and tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese sandwich) at a neighbourhood café near the hotel — around €3–4.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local workers' restaurant (restaurante popular) near Mouraria for a prato do dia — typically €7–9 for soup, main, and a drink, popular with locals and very budget-friendly.
meals.dinner: Have dinner before the Fado show at a simple Alfama tasca — try bacalhau à brás (scrambled eggs with salt cod and potato sticks) for around €10–12.

day_by_day.notes: The Museu Nacional do Azulejo is a short bus or Metro ride from the city centre (Bus 794 or 742). Monday can be a quiet day at many museums — ideal for avoiding crowds. Book Fado show seats in advance if possible, especially for popular venues, even for free or low-cost nights.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Feira da Ladra flea market at Campo de Santa Clara (open Tuesdays and Saturdays) — a fantastic free experience where locals sell antiques, vintage items, books, and curiosities. A great place to find affordable Portuguese souvenirs and soak up authentic local life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the Graça neighbourhood, one of Lisbon's most authentic and least touristy hilltop districts. Visit the Miradouro da Graça for stunning panoramic views. Explore the Igreja da Graça church (free entry) and the surrounding residential streets full of character and history.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Lisbon — return to Baixa-Chiado for a farewell walk along Rua Augusta. Enjoy a last dinner at a traditional Portuguese restaurant and pick up any remaining souvenirs. End the night with a glass of ginjinha (cherry liqueur) at one of the tiny ginjinha bars near Rossio Square for just €1.50 a shot — a quintessential Lisbon farewell tradition.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the Feira da Ladra market area — street vendors sell inexpensive snacks for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Enjoy a final budget lunch in Graça — look for a local tasca offering a prato do dia for €8–10. Try açorda (bread-based soup) or sopa de peixe (fish soup) for a truly local experience.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night at a mid-range traditional restaurant in Baixa or Chiado — a full meal with wine should still be manageable at €15–20 per person. Look for restaurants offering a tourist menu (ementa turística) for best value.

day_by_day.notes: The Feira da Ladra flea market runs from approximately 09:00 to 17:00 on Tuesdays — arrive early for the best finds. If departing the following day, begin packing in the evening and confirm transport arrangements to the airport (Metro Red Line from Alameda or Oriente stations is the most budget-friendly option at ~€1.50).

trip_options.title: Classic Lisbon, Portugal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Wander through Mouraria, Lisbon's oldest Moorish quarter and birthplace of Fado, on a self-guided or small-group food tour. Sample petiscos (Portuguese tapas) at local tascas, visit the vibrant Intendente Square, and discover street art celebrating the neighborhood's multicultural heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line) to central Lisbon. Check in to Lisbon City Stay, freshen up, and orient yourself with a short stroll around the hotel neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Baixa-Chiado district on foot — walk along Rua Augusta, cross the iconic Praça do Comércio by the Tagus River, and ride the historic Elevador de Santa Justa for panoramic rooftop views of the city. A gentle, self-guided introduction to Lisbon's layout and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Time Out Market Lisbon (Mercado da Ribeira) for dinner. Browse stalls from the city's top chefs and restaurants — try a petisco spread: grilled octopus, bacalhau croquettes, and a glass of Vinho Verde. Lively atmosphere perfect for your first night.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastel de nata at a café near the airport or upon arrival in Baixa — try Café Nicola or a local padaria (bakery).
meals.lunch: Light snack or sandwich at the hotel or a nearby café in Baixa after check-in — keep it simple on arrival day.
meals.dinner: Time Out Market Lisbon — budget €15–25 per person for a generous spread of Portuguese dishes from multiple vendors.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 90 minutes from airport to hotel including transit and check-in. The Metro Red Line connects the airport directly to downtown in ~25 minutes for about €1.65. Purchase a rechargeable Viva Viagem card for all public transport during your stay.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a traditional Portuguese breakfast at a local café — coffee and a fresh pastel de nata. Then join the Alfama District Walking Tour, exploring Lisbon's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhood. Wind through medieval alleyways, visit the Miradouro da Graça viewpoint, and learn about the city's Moorish and Christian heritage from a local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue into the Mouraria Neighborhood Food & Culture Walk — Lisbon's original Moorish quarter and the birthplace of Fado. Wander the colorful streets, discover hidden tascas (traditional taverns), and sample local street food like bifanas (pork sandwiches) and ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur) at a tiny hole-in-the-wall bar.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Alfama for a traditional Fado Show dinner experience — an intimate restaurant where live Fado music accompanies a set-menu Portuguese dinner. This is the soul of Lisbon and not to be missed. Book in advance for a table.

meals.breakfast: Café near your hotel in Baixa or Chiado — espresso (bica) and pastel de nata for under €3.
meals.lunch: Tasca in Mouraria — try a prato do dia (daily special) with soup, main, and a glass of wine for €10–14. Look for locals eating outside.
meals.dinner: Fado restaurant in Alfama such as Tasca do Chico or A Baiuca — expect €30–45 per person including food, wine, and the show. Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Alfama and Mouraria are hilly — wear comfortable walking shoes. Sunday mornings in Alfama are especially quiet and photogenic. The Fado show typically begins around 21:00; arrive 15 minutes early.

day_by_day.morning: Take Tram 15E or the train from Cais do Sodré station to Belém (about 20 minutes). Begin with the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery — a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture. Explore the ornate cloisters and the tombs of Vasco da Gama and Luís de Camões. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Tagus waterfront to the iconic Tower of Belém and the Monument to the Discoveries. Then stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery (since 1837) for the original custard tarts, dusted with cinnamon and powdered sugar — a mandatory Lisbon experience. Explore the nearby MAAT (Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology) if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon and spend the evening in the Bairro Alto neighborhood. Browse independent shops and galleries before settling in for dinner at a traditional restaurant. Afterward, enjoy the neighborhood's lively bar scene for a nightcap of Portuguese wine or craft beer.

meals.breakfast: Grab coffee and a croissant before heading to Belém, or eat at a café near Cais do Sodré station.
meals.lunch: Pastéis de Belém for tarts (€1.50 each) plus a light lunch at a riverside café in Belém — grilled fish or a bifana sandwich for €10–15.
meals.dinner: Bairro Alto restaurant — try Taberna da Rua das Flores or a similar tasca for traditional petiscos and wine; €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Jerónimos Monastery is closed on Mondays — if this applies, swap with the Tower of Belém exterior and MAAT, or check updated opening hours closer to travel. Tram 15E runs frequently from Praça da Figueira. The Belém waterfront is lovely for an afternoon walk.

day_by_day.morning: Take the early train from Rossio Station to Sintra (40 minutes, ~€2.30 each way). Begin with Pena Palace — a vibrant Romanticist palace perched dramatically on a forested hilltop with stunning views over the Atlantic. Arrive by 10:00 to avoid midday crowds. The colorful architecture and surrounding National Park are unlike anything in Lisbon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the grounds of Sintra — visit the Moorish Castle ruins for sweeping panoramic views, then wander the charming village center. Browse the local shops for queijadas de Sintra (traditional cheese pastries) and travesseiros (almond and egg pastries) from Piriquita bakery, a Sintra institution since 1862.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lisbon by early evening (trains run frequently). Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the Príncipe Real neighborhood — one of Lisbon's most elegant and food-forward areas. Browse the Saturday antique market stalls if open, and enjoy a quieter evening compared to the busier tourist zones.

meals.breakfast: Quick café breakfast near Rossio Station before catching the train — coffee and toast or a pastry for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Sintra village restaurant — try a regional lunch with local wine at a mid-range spot for €15–20. Avoid the most tourist-heavy terraces and look for spots with Portuguese menus.
meals.dinner: Príncipe Real restaurant — try O Corvo or a similar neighborhood gem for creative Portuguese cuisine; €25–35 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a combined Sintra palace ticket online in advance to save time queuing — Pena Palace + Moorish Castle combo is around €20. Wear layers as Sintra can be cooler and mistier than Lisbon even in May. The last train back to Lisbon runs late, but aim to return by 19:00 for a comfortable evening.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit any Lisbon highlights you missed or spend a leisurely morning at the Mercado de Campo de Ourique — a beloved neighborhood market hall with local food vendors, fresh produce, and a relaxed local atmosphere far from the tourist trail. Ideal for a slow breakfast or brunch with locals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) — one of Lisbon's most unique and underrated museums, housed in a 16th-century convent. Discover the history of Portugal's iconic azulejo tiles across stunning galleries. Afterward, explore the LX Factory — a creative hub in a repurposed industrial complex with independent shops, street art, and cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Lisbon — return to the Chiado or Cais do Sodré area for a celebratory meal at a restaurant with a full Portuguese tasting experience: bacalhau à brás, caldo verde soup, and a bottle of Alentejo red wine. End the night with a stroll along the Tagus waterfront and a final ginjinha at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Mercado de Campo de Ourique — fresh bread, local cheese, charcuterie, and coffee from market vendors for €5–8.
meals.lunch: LX Factory café or restaurant — creative light lunch with a Portuguese twist; €12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Chiado or Cais do Sodré — splurge slightly on your last night at a well-regarded restaurant like Cantinho do Avillez or similar; €30–40 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: The National Tile Museum is a 15-minute Uber or taxi ride from the city center (~€7). LX Factory is especially vibrant on Sundays but worth visiting any day. Pack the night before if your departure is early the next morning. Keep your Viva Viagem card topped up for any final transit needs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged to Lisbon City Stay hotel. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your luxury accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely orientation stroll through the Chiado and Bairro Alto neighborhoods near the hotel. Browse elegant boutiques, admire the Art Nouveau architecture, and stop at the iconic A Brasileira café for a bica (espresso) — one of Lisbon's most storied literary cafés dating back to 1905.
day_by_day.evening: Mouraria Neighborhood Food & Culture Walk — ease into Lisbon's soul with a guided evening wander through Mouraria, the Moorish quarter and birthplace of Fado. Soak in the atmospheric tiled streets, hear the first echoes of Fado music drifting from doorways, and discover hidden local gems before a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light snack or coffee on arrival at the airport lounge or upon hotel check-in — the hotel's welcome amenities will suffice.
meals.lunch: N/A (in transit) — grab a light bite at the airport or upon arrival at the hotel's lounge.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Belcanto (2 Michelin stars, Chef José Avillez) — Lisbon's most celebrated fine-dining restaurant in Chiado. Expect modern Portuguese haute cuisine with impeccable wine pairings. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private luxury transfer from Lisbon Humberto Delgado Airport in advance. Ask the hotel concierge to confirm Belcanto reservation upon check-in. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show (morning portion) — join a premium guided walking tour through Alfama, Lisbon's oldest medieval neighborhood. Explore narrow cobblestone alleyways, visit the São Jorge Castle for panoramic city views, and discover hidden miradouros (viewpoints) like Portas do Sol with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Alfama experience by visiting the National Pantheon (Igreja de Santa Engrácia) and the Santa Apolónia antique market if running on weekends. Afterwards, take a vintage Tram 28 ride through the historic districts — a quintessential Lisbon experience — before returning to the hotel for a brief rest.
day_by_day.evening: Fado Show at a premium Casa de Fado — attend an intimate, world-class Fado performance at Clube de Fado or Sr. Vinho, both legendary venues in Alfama. Dinner and Fado are combined in a multi-course dinner experience with Portuguese wines, creating an unforgettable cultural evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Café de São Bento — a classic Lisbon breakfast of tosta mista, fresh orange juice, and a galão (milky espresso).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Chapitô à Mesa, a stylish restaurant perched above Alfama with sweeping views of the Tagus River. Try the bacalhau à brás (codfish) or grilled sea bass.
meals.dinner: Dinner included as part of the Fado show experience at Clube de Fado — a curated Portuguese menu with regional wines paired with live Fado performances by renowned fadistas.

day_by_day.notes: Book the premium Fado dinner show well in advance as top venues sell out quickly, especially on weekends. Wear smart-casual attire for the Fado house. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for Alfama's cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical Landmarks & Pastéis de Belém — take a private chauffeured car to the historic Belém district (15 minutes from central Lisbon). Begin with a guided visit to the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture built in the 16th century. Explore the ornate cloisters and the tomb of explorer Vasco da Gama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Tower of Belém (Torre de Belém), a fortified tower standing at the edge of the Tagus River and another UNESCO World Heritage Site. Afterwards, stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery — the original home of the pastel de nata (custard tart) since 1837 — for the most authentic tart in Portugal, dusted with cinnamon and powdered sugar. Also visit the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos) for a panoramic rooftop view.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon. Enjoy a sunset aperitivo at TOPO Chiado rooftop bar with sweeping views over the city's terracotta rooftops and the Tagus. Follow with a sophisticated dinner in the Príncipe Real neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit Padaria Portuguesa for fresh pastries, avocado toast, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Feitoria Restaurant (1 Michelin star) in Belém — Chef João Rodrigues crafts exceptional modern Portuguese cuisine inspired by local producers. Stunning riverside setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alma (1 Michelin star, Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa) in Chiado — refined contemporary Portuguese cuisine with an outstanding wine list featuring the best of Douro, Alentejo, and Dão regions.

day_by_day.notes: Belém is best visited on Sunday mornings when crowds are lighter. The Jerónimos Monastery is closed on Mondays, so Sunday is ideal. A private guide for Belém adds significant depth to the historical experience.

day_by_day.morning: Sintra Royal Palaces Day Trip — depart early by private chauffeured car to the fairy-tale UNESCO World Heritage town of Sintra (40 minutes from Lisbon). Begin with a guided visit to the magnificent Pena Palace, a Romanticist castle perched atop the Sintra Mountains with its vivid colors and eclectic architecture. Explore the surrounding forested park with sweeping Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Moorish Castle (Castelo dos Mouros), a medieval hilltop fortress with dramatic ramparts and panoramic vistas over Sintra's lush valleys. Optionally visit the mystical Quinta da Regaleira, known for its initiation wells and Masonic symbolism. Explore Sintra's charming village center and sample local sweets — travesseiros (almond and egg pastries) from Piriquita bakery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lisbon by late afternoon. Spend the evening at leisure — enjoy a relaxing treatment at the hotel spa if available, followed by a refined dinner in the Avenida da Liberdade area, Lisbon's most elegant boulevard.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure to Sintra.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Incomum by Luis Santos in Sintra village — a charming fine-dining restaurant serving creative Portuguese cuisine with local Sintra ingredients in an elegant setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eleven Restaurant (1 Michelin star) — panoramic views over Lisbon from the top of Parque Eduardo VII, with sophisticated contemporary European-Portuguese cuisine and an exceptional wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Sintra involves significant walking on uneven terrain and steep hills — wear comfortable but stylish walking shoes. Book Pena Palace tickets in advance online to avoid queues. A private guide for Sintra is highly recommended to unlock the full historical narrative of the palaces.

day_by_day.morning: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — spend a culinary morning at the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré, widely regarded as one of the world's best food markets. Sample an expertly curated selection of Portuguese cuisine: petiscos (tapas), fresh seafood, artisan cheeses, charcuterie, ginjinha (cherry liqueur), and premium pastéis de nata. A local food expert guide can be arranged for a deeper tasting journey through Portugal's gastronomic regions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu Nacional do Azulejo (National Tile Museum) — housed in a stunning 16th-century convent, this world-class museum traces the history of Portugal's iconic azulejo (ceramic tile) tradition from Moorish origins to contemporary art. A deeply immersive cultural experience. Afterwards, browse the elegant boutiques of Príncipe Real for artisan souvenirs — premium Portuguese ceramics, wines, and cork goods.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening in Lisbon — return to the Chiado or Bairro Alto for a final sunset at Miradouro de Santa Catarina (Adamastor viewpoint) with a glass of local vinho verde in hand. End the trip with a spectacular farewell dinner at one of Lisbon's finest tables.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast or grab a pastel de nata and galão at a neighborhood café before heading to Time Out Market.
meals.lunch: Tasting lunch at Time Out Market — graze across multiple premium stalls: fresh oysters from Alexandre Silva, octopus rice from Marlene Vieira, and petiscos from Henrique Sá Pessoa's stall.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Loco (1 Michelin star, Chef Alexandre Silva) — one of Lisbon's most avant-garde and exciting tasting menu experiences, blending Portuguese heritage with bold contemporary techniques. An extraordinary final night in Lisbon.

day_by_day.notes: Time Out Market is best visited on weekday mornings to avoid weekend crowds. The Azulejo Museum requires approximately 2 hours and is a must for history lovers. Pack any purchased wines or ceramics carefully for the return journey. Confirm departure logistics with the hotel concierge for the following day.
